title: Guarder: A Stable and Lightweight Reconfigurable RRAM-based PIM Accelerator for DNN IP Protection
problem: RRAM-based processing-in-memory accelerators suffer from imprecise weights due to programming stochasticity, limiting model accuracy, and cannot effectively utilize conventional weight encryption/decryption IP protection schemes.
motivation: RRAM PIM offers energy-efficient DNN inference, but reliability and IP protection are critical barriers to deployment.
method: Guarder proposes a software-hardware co-design: (1) Hardware: 3T2R cells for reliable MAC operations and reconfigurable inverter operating voltages to encode encryption keys directly in RRAM, (2) Software: Contrastive training ensures high accuracy on authorized chips and degraded performance on unauthorized ones.
key_novelty: Co-designed 3T2R RRAM PIM with encrypted-key inverter voltage encoding and contrastive training for DNN IP protection.
contributions: 3T2R RRAM cells for reliable MAC operations reducing programming stochasticity effects
Reconfigurable inverter operating voltages for in-device encryption key encoding
Contrastive training method ensuring performance gap between authorized and unauthorized chips
1.41× area reduction, 2.28× energy reduction vs traditional RRAM accelerators
Validated on image classification (MLP, ResNet, ViT), segmentation (SegFormer), and generation (DiT)
limitations: IP protection scheme limited to hardware-level encryption; software-level attacks and key recovery resilience not discussed.
primary_theme: encrypted-RRAM PIM accelerator for DNN IP protection
